chapter_title: Orienting Yourself: The Use of Coordinates
key_takeaways: A point's position in 2D space requires two perpendicular reference lines, defined relative to origin (0,0).
Points on the x-axis have coordinates (x, 0), while points on the y-axis have coordinates (0, y).
Order matters in coordinates: (x, y) != (y, x) unless x = y.
Geometrical distance between any two points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) is derived directly from the Baudhāyana-Pythagoras theorem as sqrt((x2 - x1)^2 + (y2 - y1)^2).
Reflection of point (x, y) across y-axis yields (-x, y), and across x-axis yields (x, -y), preserving lengths and shapes.
Algebraic representations allow pinpoint accurate geometric proofs and real-world spatial planning (such as architectural layout analysis).
